title: YC founder asks desperate job seekers to tattoo themselves for an interview
excerpt: LemonLime’s Jordan Zietz said he’s really, really sorry about the whole thing.
content_html:
Today in novel sentences: A San Francisco AI startup CEO is apologizing for asking people to permanently tattoo themselves in exchange for a job interview.

One of San Francisco’s many difficult-to-explain AI startups, LemonLime, recently offered hopeful (desperate?) applicants an instant job interview, but only if they got its logo or a related design permanently tattooed on their bodies. 

Seven people took the company up on the offer, according to CEO Jordan Zietz. The logo resembles a wedge of lemon, or perhaps Pac-Man mid-bite — a permanent reminder of a company that, according to its website, “learns your business and then automates your team’s busywork in a single click.”

“We hosted a YC Startup School afterparty at the LemonLime office to meet exceptional people, and find out which of them are just as crazy as we are,” Zietz wrote Tuesday in an upbeat LinkedIn post that for obvious reasons has been deleted. “That’s why we brought an actual tattoo artist to our party and offered an instant interview to anyone who got a LemonLime tattoo. We are bold, we take risks, and we do things that haven’t been done before.”

This new citrus flavor of corporate branding was immediately beset by detractors who are clearly not in founder mode. 

“Since your advisers and investors seem to be asleep at the wheel, here is some Silicon Valley startup advice: Predicating job interviews on getting a tattoo is abhorrent and invites litigation,” one representative commented in response to the LinkedIn post. 

Zietz agreed to a phone interview Wednesday morning to explain his thinking but backed out minutes before, texting, “slammed w things rn, sorry :(” 

A few hours prior, he posted a public apology, saying he had “messed up” and that participants chose their own tattoos. He claimed he would pay for tattoo removal services. 

“Regardless of said intent, turning a celebration of personalized art into a company stunt was poorly exercised judgement,” Zietz wrote on X (opens in new tab), claiming that everyone got an interview regardless of whether they were inked. 

Over text, Zietz said none of the attendees received a logo as a tattoo, despite what he’d said in the LinkedIn post.

One attendee contradicted his claim. “Yes, almost everyone else got a LemonLime logo tattoo,” Dimple Amitha Garuadapuri (opens in new tab)posted on X (opens in new tab). She said she got a tattoo at the event that was not the LemonLime logo but didn’t respond when asked what it depicted.

“100% incorrect,” Zietz told The Standard about Garuadapuri’s logo claim.

Another attendee said he saw at least one participant tattooed with a lemon. 

LemonLime is a graduate of Y Combinator, an accelerator known for anointing dozens of small companies a year with $500,000 checks, networking opportunities, and Garry Tan’s personal phone number. 

Some graduates have gone on to become blockbuster companies like Reddit and Airbnb, but the remaining chaff often resort to desperate marketing ploys to set themselves apart. Remember those “Stop hiring humans” billboards blanketing San Francisco? That was a YC company. 

LemonLime bills itself as a no-code AI startup, not to be confused with the hundreds of startups building something similar. Aside from the $500,000 from Y Combinator, it doesn’t appear to have additional funding. 

Still, maybe permanent branding is the ticket to the YC mafia. The founder of Corgi, a YC insurance tech company with a $4 billion reported valuation, known for running a Corgi cafe without any dogs, recently said (opens in new tab) that two-thirds of his early staff members have a company tattoo.

content_html_zh:
今天，用新颖的句子来说：旧金山一家人工智能初创公司的首席执行官为要求人们永久纹身以换取工作面试而道歉。

LemonLime 是旧金山众多难以解释的人工智能初创公司之一，最近提出了充满希望（绝望？） 申请人可以立即获得面试机会，但前提是他们的标志或相关设计永久纹在身上。

首席执行官乔丹·齐茨 (Jordan Zietz) 表示，有七个人接受了该公司的提议。 该标志类似于一块柠檬，或者可能是吃豆人的中间咬一口——永久提醒人们一家公司，根据其网站，“了解你的业务，然后只需单击一下即可自动化你团队的繁忙工作。”

“我们在 LemonLime 办公室举办了一场 YC 创业学校余兴派对，以结识杰出人士，并找出他们中哪些人和我们一样疯狂，”Zietz 周二在 LinkedIn 上发表的一篇乐观的帖子中写道，该帖子由于显而易见的原因已被删除。 “这就是为什么我们邀请了一位真正的纹身艺术家来参加我们的聚会，并为任何有 LemonLime 纹身的人提供即时采访。 我们大胆，我们敢于冒险，我们做以前从未做过的事情。”

这种新的柑橘风味的企业品牌立即受到批评者的困扰，他们显然不处于创始人模式。

“既然你的顾问和投资者似乎在开车时睡着了，这里有一些硅谷初创公司的建议：以纹身为前提来预测工作面试是令人厌恶的，并且会引发诉讼，”一位代表在回复 LinkedIn 帖子时评论道。

齐茨同意周三早上接受电话采访，解释他的想法，但几分钟前又退出了，发短信说，“猛烈抨击事情，抱歉:(”

几个小时前，他发布了公开道歉，称他“搞砸了”，参与者选择了自己的纹身。 他声称他会支付纹身去除服务的费用。

“无论意图如何，将个性化艺术的庆祝变成公司的噱头都是缺乏判断力的做法，”齐茨在 X 上写道（在新选项卡中打开），声称每个人都得到了采访，无论他们是否有纹身。

齐茨通过短信表示，尽管他在 LinkedIn 帖子中说了些什么，但没有一个与会者收到了徽标纹身。

一位与会者反驳了他的说法。 “是的，几乎每个人都有 LemonLime 标志纹身，”Dimple Amitha Garuadapuri（在新选项卡中打开）在 X（在新选项卡中打开）上发布。 她说她在活动中纹了一个不是 LemonLime 标志的纹身，但当被问及它描绘的是什么时她没有回应。

“100%不正确，”齐茨在接受《标准报》采访时谈到 Garuadapuri 的标志说法。

另一位与会者表示，他看到至少一名与会者身上纹有柠檬。

LemonLime 是 Y Combinator 的毕业生，Y Combinator 是一家加速器，以每年为数十家小公司提供 50 万美元的支票、社交机会和 Garry Tan 的个人电话号码而闻名。

一些毕业生后来成为 Reddit 和 Airbnb 等轰动一时的公司，但剩下的人往往会采取绝望的营销策略来使自己与众不同。 还记得那些覆盖旧金山的“停止雇用人类”广告牌吗？ 那是一家YC公司。

LemonLime 将自己标榜为一家无代码人工智能初创公司，不要与数百家构建类似产品的初创公司混淆。 除了 Y Combinator 提供的 50 万美元之外，它似乎没有额外的资金。

尽管如此，也许永久品牌是 YC 黑手党的门票。 Corgi 是一家 YC 保险科技公司，估值为 40 亿美元，该公司以经营一家没有狗的柯基咖啡馆而闻名，最近表示（在新选项卡中打开）他的三分之二早期员工都有公司纹身。
